Invariance and y-increments give integral x=0; stationary square of x yields a²=(r²-1)E[x²]-r²E[x² sin²(dy)], impossible for r<=1. A bounded forward orbit would produce a compactly supported invariant empirical limit, so none exists. For r<1, u_n=x_n/a obeys u_{n+1}=1+kappa_n u_n, |kappa_n|<=r; boundedness and squared telescoping plus Jensen force every mean accumulation in [1/(1+r),1/(1-r)], hence y drifts linearly. Phase-locked examples attain both bounds. On a primitive 2cycle, x1=-x0 and B0+B1=-2 imply |x0|>=|a|/(r-1); the stated explicit phase pair attains equality for each r>1 with adapted e. An independently coded check reconstructed seven period-two and multiple phase-locked examples; finite checks do not prove universal invariant-measure statements.
